papers.title_in_file: Can Entanglement-enhanced Quantum Kernels Improve Data Classification?
papers.version_note: arXiv:2406.01948v1 [quant-ph], 4 Jun 2024. The text layer ends the Conclusion and the Experimental section out of order across page breaks (the sentence 'IBM ... computing platform.' is split by a page footer); the content was read in full.
papers.what_it_is: A short empirical preprint that trains a Qiskit quantum SVM (ZZFeatureMap, fidelity kernel) and a classical baseline on a sensor-acquired respiratory dataset, the Wisconsin breast cancer dataset and the Iris dataset, and reports about 45% higher accuracy for the quantum model on the respiratory data.

existing.note: The abstract and the Conclusion say this. The paper varies the wording: the Introduction says '45% higher precision', the Conclusion says 'over 45% higher accuracy'. The text never gives the per-model accuracy numbers (they are in the Figure 4b table image) and never says whether 45% is percentage points or a relative gain; see the new assertions.
quotes: Compared to classical algorithms, our findings reveal that QSVM performs better with higher accuracy 45% for complex respiratory data sets while maintaining comparable performance with linear datasets

existing.note: The value is right. The stored anchor says Section III discussion; the sentence is in Section II (Methods), at the end of the equations, p.3. The paper states it as an attribution and does not test it (no ablation against a non-entangled map is reported).
quotes: The higher accuracy of the quantum SVM is attributed to the entangled quantum states effectively mapping data to a much higher-dimensional space compared to classical or nonentangled quantum mappings
existing.reader_inference: No experiment in the paper compares an entangled map against a non-entangled quantum map, so the attribution is not tested.

assertions.value: The authors report that the kernel-enhanced QSVM performed more accurately, with 45 % higher accuracy, on the randomly acquired respiratory dataset, with almost comparable performance on the breast cancer dataset.
quotes: The QSVM enhanced with the kernel has been found to perform more accurately with 45 % higher accuracy for the randomly acquired respiratory dataset while providing almost comparable performance for the separate classes of the breast cancer dataset.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study; the per-model accuracy values are only in the Figure 4b table image.
assertions.reader_inference: The text does not say whether 45 % means percentage points or a relative gain, and gives neither model's accuracy, so the size of the gap cannot be checked from the text.

assertions.value: The authors describe the 45% gain as 'higher precision' in the Introduction, as 'higher accuracy' in the Abstract, Results and Conclusion, and as 'over 45%' in the Conclusion.
assertions.anchor: Section I p.2; Section IV p.5-6
quotes: our research validates the superior performance of KQ-SVM, 45% higher precision than its classical counterparts.
achieving over 45% higher accuracy on complex datasets while maintaining comparable performance on linear datasets.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study; the metric is named inconsistently.
assertions.reader_inference: Precision and accuracy are different metrics, and 'over 45%' is not the same figure as '45%'; the headline number is not pinned to one metric in the text.

assertions.value: The authors conclude that empirical analysis across diverse datasets shows KQ-SVM significantly outperforms classical SVMs, with over 45% higher accuracy on complex datasets and comparable performance on linear datasets.
quotes: Empirical analysis across diverse datasets shows KQ-SVM significantly outperforms classical SVMs, achieving over 45% higher accuracy on complex datasets while maintaining comparable performance on linear datasets.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own conclusion from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper reports no significance test, no repeated runs and no confidence interval, and no dataset size, so 'significantly' is not backed by a statistic in the text.

assertions.value: The authors state that a quantum circuit of 2 qubits, comprising two Hadamard gates to create the entanglement and two poly x-gates, was used to perform the quantum measurement of both the respiratory and breast cancer datasets.
quotes: A quantum circuit of 2 qubits comprising the two Hadamard gates to create the entanglement and two ploy x-gates has been utilized to perform the quantum measurement of both datasets
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own experimental setup, Section III.
assertions.reader_inference: A circuit of Hadamard gates followed by single-qubit rotations creates no entanglement by itself; the entangling gate is not named here. Section V names the ZZFeatureMap, which does entangle, so the two descriptions of the circuit differ.

assertions.value: The authors state that the study used the breast cancer, Iris and randomly generated respiratory datasets; the respiratory data were a random dataset of different breathings acquired by a piezoelectric sensor, the breast cancer dataset was taken as a linear dataset, and the Wisconsin Breast Cancer (Diagnostic) data came from the UCI Machine Learning Repository.
assertions.anchor: Section I p.1-2; Section III p.4; Section V.C p.6
quotes: we used QSVM to classify the random dataset of different breathings acquired by the piezoelectric sensor.
The breast cancer dataset has been taken as a linear dataset, where the two classes are distinguishable
The Wisconsin Breast Cancer (Diagnostic) dataset is obtained from the UCI Machine Learning Repository.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of the datasets it used, Sections I, III and V.C.
assertions.reader_inference: The respiratory data are called 'randomly generated' in one place and 'randomly acquired' in another; the text never says how many recordings, samples or features there are, so the dataset size is unknown from the text.

assertions.value: The authors state that respiratory signals were acquired with a digital storage oscilloscope (Keysight DSOX1102G) from a piezoelectric sensor, in the non-invasive mode on the author himself and volunteers, with written consent.
quotes: A digital storage oscilloscope (DSOX1102G, Keysight) was used to acquire the open-circuit voltage and respiratory signals.
All the measurements were acquired in the non-invasive mode on the author himself and volunteers.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of how its respiratory data were acquired, Section V.B.
assertions.reader_inference: The number of volunteers and the length and labeling of the recordings are not stated in the text.

assertions.value: The authors state that the Iris dataset with 3 classes was used to go beyond binary classification, with a 4-qubit circuit that uses Hadamard gates to create the entanglement.
quotes: To extend our investigation to more than binary classes, we have utilized the Iris dataset having 3 classes.
The 4-qubit quantum circuit consists of a 4hadammard gate to create the entanglement
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup for the Iris experiment, Section III.
assertions.reader_inference: No Iris accuracy for the quantum or the classical model is given in the text; Figure 4b is said to hold the Iris metrics.

assertions.value: The authors report that for the Iris data the quantum circuit's training accuracy increased as the depth of the circuit increased, which they read as the ability to grasp more refined patterns.
quotes: The quantum circuit learning journey shows an increase in the training accuracy as the depth of the circuit increases, indicating its ability to grasp more refined patterns in the data
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study; training accuracy only, shown in a figure.
assertions.reader_inference: Only training accuracy is shown against depth; no test accuracy is reported against depth.

assertions.value: The authors state that the increased accuracy in Figure 3b prompts further investigation to confirm whether it indicates successful information extraction or potential overfitting.
quotes: The increased accuracy in Figure 3b prompts further investigation to confirm whether it indicates successful information extraction or potential overfitting.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement that overfitting is not ruled out, Section III.

assertions.value: The authors state that, in the Iris scatter plot, the lack of clear labeling obscures the specific attributes used for classification, making precise interpretations difficult to find.
quotes: However, the lack of clear labeling obscures the specific attributes used for classification, making precise interpretations difficult to find.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of a limit of its figure, Section III.

assertions.value: The authors report, for the kernel and learning-rate experiment, that the RBF kernel with a learning rate of 0.01 had the highest accuracy, 80%, on the training data but the lowest, 30%, on the testing data, which they read as potential overfitting.
quotes: the RBF kernel with a learning rate of 0.01 exhibited the highest accuracy of 80% on the training data but the lowest accuracy
of 30% on the testing data, indicating potential overfitting.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The text does not name the dataset or say whether this is the classical SVM or the quantum model. The caption of Figure 4a says 'support vector machine (SVM)'. A learning rate is not a parameter of a standard kernel SVM, which fits the neural-network style baseline described in Section V.C.2.

assertions.value: The authors report that the linear kernel with a learning rate of 0.5 achieved the best test accuracy, 60%, with a lower training accuracy of 57%, which they read as potential underfitting.
quotes: the linear kernel with a learning rate of 0.5 achieved the best performance on the test data with an accuracy of 60%
However, it showed a lower accuracy of 57% in the training data, indicating potential underfitting.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The best test accuracy in this experiment is 60%, near chance for a two-class problem; the dataset is not named.

assertions.value: The authors report that the polynomial kernel reached 53% on the training data and 50% on the testing data, and the sigmoid kernel reached 48% accuracy on the training data and 40% on the testing data.
quotes: the polynomial kernel achieving 53% precision on the training data and 50% in the testing data, and the sigmoid kernel achieving 48% accuracy on the training data and 40% on the testing data.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The text calls the polynomial figure 'precision' and the sigmoid figure 'accuracy' in the same sentence, so the metric is unclear.

assertions.value: The authors state that the choice of kernel and learning rate significantly influences model performance and that the optimal choice depends on the specific problem and the data set.
quotes: The findings revealed that the choice of kernel and learning rate significantly influences model performance.
The optimal choice depends on the specific problem and the data set, emphasizing the need for experimentation to identify the best combination for a given task.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' reading of one experiment.

assertions.value: The authors state that the evaluation metrics (precision, recall and F1 score) in the summary table, compared across the Iris (i), respiratory (r) and breast cancer (b) datasets, show not much deviation in accuracy between classical and quantum algorithms on the linear data, while on the random datasets quantum machine learning performs better with higher accuracy 45%.
quotes: there is not much deviation in accuracy when training the linear data, while for the random datasets, quantum machine learning performs better with higher accuracy 45% (Figure 4b).
where i indicates the iris data set, r indicates the randomly generated respiratory dataset, while b represents the breast cancer data set.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study; the table is an image.
assertions.reader_inference: The text says 'precision' twice in its list of metrics, so the metric list is garbled; the table values are not in the text layer.

assertions.value: The authors state that the quantum model used the ZZFeatureMap from Qiskit's circuit library, a fidelity quantum kernel from Qiskit Machine Learning, and the QSVC model; the classical comparison was a scikit-learn Support Vector Classifier (SVC).
quotes: Our quantum-based model consisted of feature mapping using the ZZFeatureMap from Qiskit’s circuit library, a fidelity quantum kernel implemented using the Fidelity Quantum Kernel from Qiskit Machine Learning, and the QSVC model for training and classification tasks.
For comparison, we trained a classical Support Vector Classifier (SVC) using scikit-learn.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own implementation, Section V.C.1.
assertions.reader_inference: Section V.C.2 describes a different classical model (see babu-classical-baseline-setup); the text does not say which baseline produced the 45% comparison.

assertions.value: The authors state that they used a fixed random seed and split the data into training and testing sets with an 80:20 ratio using stratified sampling, and that all the quantum measurements were carried out on an IBM computing platform.
quotes: We initialized the experiment with a fixed random seed for reproducibility and split the data set into training and testing sets with an 80:20 ratio using stratified sampling.
All the quantum measurements have been carried out on the IBM
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup, Section V.C.1.
assertions.reader_inference: The text does not say whether the IBM platform was real hardware or a simulator, nor the shot count, nor whether noise was present. The text layer puts the words 'computing platform.' on a later line.

assertions.value: The authors state that the classical SVM was built with NumPy, TensorFlow and Matplotlib, with one-hot encoded labels and an 80% training and 20% testing split, trained for 10 epochs with batch size 32 using categorical crossentropy loss and the Adam optimizer.
quotes: Support vector machine (SVM) has been built using Python libraries, including (NumPy, TensorFlow, and Matplotlib), and sequential data for a classification task.
split the data set into 80% training and 20% testing.
It was trained for 10 epochs with batch size 32, using categorical crossentropy loss and the Adam optimizer.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own classical baseline, Section V.C.2.
assertions.reader_inference: Epochs, batch size, cross-entropy loss and Adam describe a gradient-trained neural-network style model, not a standard kernel SVM; no hyperparameter tuning of the baseline is described, so the 45% comparison may reflect a weak baseline.

assertions.value: The authors define the quantum kernel as the squared magnitude of the inner product of two quantum feature states, and the entanglement-enhanced quantum kernel in the same form with the entangled state obtained by applying Ue(x), an entanglement based on the input x, to an entangled state.
quotes: Kq(xi, xj) = |⟨ϕq(xi)|ϕq(xj)⟩|2
|ϕq,e(x)⟩ = Ue(x)|entangled state⟩
Where Ue(x) is an entanglement based on the input x.
Kq,e(xi, xj ) = |⟨ϕq,e(xi)|ϕq,e(xj )⟩|2
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's definitions of its kernels in Section II, Eqs. 7, 11 and 12; the exponent at the end of Eqs. 7 and 12 is printed flat and is a square.
assertions.reader_inference: The 'entangled state' and the form of Ue(x) are not specified in the equations; the entanglement-enhanced kernel has the same form as the plain fidelity kernel, so the entangling content is only in the state definition.

assertions.value: The authors state that quantum feature maps embed data into an exponentially larger space, enabling better separation of complex data distributions, and that entangled states represent dependencies between features more effectively than classical methods.
quotes: Quantum feature maps embed data into an exponentially larger space, enabling better separation of complex data distributions:
Entangled states represent dependencies between features more effectively than classical methods
assertions.certainty_reason: An author's claim stated without proof or experiment in the paper.
assertions.reader_inference: A larger Hilbert space alone does not imply better separation; the paper gives no argument or test for this.

assertions.value: The authors state that quantum algorithms, particularly quantum Support Vector Machines, demonstrate superiority, especially when dealing with random datasets, and that the ZZ feature map plays a crucial role in transforming random data into a higher-dimensional space, thereby enhancing the training of QSVM compared with classical SVM.
assertions.anchor: Section I p.2; Section II p.2
quotes: quantum algorithms, particularly quantum Support Vector Machines (SVM), demonstrate superiority, especially when dealing with random datasets.

The ZZ feature map of Quantum Support Vector Machines (QSVM) plays a crucial role in transforming random data into a higher-dimensional space, thereby enhancing the training of QSVM in comparison to classical SVM.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author's claim stated in the framing text without a test in the paper.
assertions.reader_inference: Superiority is stated before the results and is not defined for 'random' data; the paper never defines what makes a dataset 'random'.

assertions.value: The authors state, citing reference 16, that quantum SVM offers a significant speed-up gain in overall run-time complexity compared with classical counterparts; the paper reports no run-time measurement of its own.
quotes: Quantum SVM offers a significant speed-up gain in overall run-time complexity compared to their classical counterparts. [16]
assertions.certainty_reason: A result the paper attributes to other work (reference 16).
assertions.reader_inference: No timing or complexity result appears anywhere in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors state in the Abstract that quantum machine learning algorithms offer significant advantages, including exponentially faster computations, enhanced data handling capabilities, inherent parallelism, and improved optimization for complex problems.
quotes: quantum machine learning algorithms offer significant advantages, including exponentially faster computations, enhanced data handling capabilities, inherent parallelism, and improved optimization for complex problems.
assertions.certainty_reason: A general claim without evidence in the paper.
assertions.reader_inference: The experiments here are 2-qubit and 4-qubit circuits; nothing in them measures speed or scaling.

assertions.value: The authors state that the research demonstrates the transformative potential of quantum computing in machine learning, paving the way for enhanced performance and accuracy in real-world applications.
quotes: This research demonstrates the transformative potential of quantum computing in machine learning, paving the way for enhanced performance and accuracy in real-world applications.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author's claim; the experiments are small and use few qubits.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper has no dedicated limitations section.
